name: mem_profile
description: A first pass over a memory file's header and a sample of its bytes, before anything is run against it. Names the container only when the header says so (Windows crash dump with its physical-memory run list, checked for order, overlap and payload size; LiME with every range it frames; hibernation file; ELF core with its byte order from e_ident; AVML by its first four bytes), and says "unrecognised" for anything else, which is what a flat capture looks like and also what a file that is not memory looks like. It is not validation: it does not decode hibernation or AVML framing, does not enumerate an ELF core's segments, and does not establish the architecture, the captured ranges or the completeness of a capture. Operating-system and structure hints are signature counts in a sample of the head, middle and tail (sampled_ranges lists the bytes actually read, each range scanned on its own), not counts for the file. file_pages_4k_estimate is the file length over 4096, not a count of captured pages. A crash dump's SystemTime is given raw (system_time_filetime, 100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 UTC) beside the ISO 8601 time with its seven fractional digits, and a value that is not a time (past the year 9999) is named in problems with its raw value, not turned into null.

path.description: The memory image, dump or hibernation file

scan_mb.description: How many megabytes to sample for operating-system and structure hints (default 64, at most 4096); the answer lists the ranges actually read
